'''Swechha''' (registered as the '''Swechha We For Change Foundation''') is an
environmental and youth organisation based in [[New Delhi]], India. It began in
2000 as ''We for Yamuna'', a volunteer campaign against the pollution of the
[[Yamuna|river Yamuna]] in Delhi, and has since worked on school and college
environmental education, tree planting, waste and upcycling enterprises, and
experiential journeys along the Yamuna and into rural India.<ref name="twl" /><ref name="cnnbio" /><ref name="about" />

The organisation was founded by Vimlendu Jha, who continues to lead it. Its work
on the Yamuna, and Jha's own campaigning and documentary films about the river,
brought international attention: in 2007 he was one of six people worldwide
chosen for [[CNN International]]'s ''Be the Change'' series, which followed his
work on the river over the following year.<ref name="cnnbio" /><ref name="cnnriver" /><ref name="cnnarchive" />
The name ''swechha'' is a [[Sanskrit]]-derived word meaning "of one's own free
will".<ref name="about" />

== History ==

=== We for Yamuna (2000) ===
Vimlendu Jha, then a student at [[St. Stephen's College, Delhi]], began looking
at the condition of the Yamuna in Delhi in the late 1990s. After about two years
of research he and a group of friends started ''We for Yamuna'' on 14 August
2000, holding street plays and awareness events — including at [[Dilli Haat]] —
about a river that supplies much of the city's water and receives much of its
sewage. Several hundred young people joined the early campaign.<ref name="twl" /><ref name="lokmarg" />
Swechha describes the campaign as "a collective response towards growing apathy
towards one of the most polluted rivers of the world".<ref name="about" />

The group was registered as an organisation in 2001 and took the name
Swechha.<ref name="twl" /> Its office, in Khirki Extension in south Delhi, was
built largely from waste and reclaimed materials.<ref name="twl" /><ref name="lbb" />

=== Expansion (2004 onwards) ===
In 2004 Swechha ran the first ''Yamuna Yatra'', a twelve-day journey tracing the
Yamuna from its source at [[Yamunotri]] to [[Agra]], which became the
organisation's best-known programme and was reported in the Delhi press at the
time.<ref name="tribune2004" /><ref name="about" /> Through the 2000s the
organisation broadened from river campaigning into school and college
programmes, tree planting, and work with children living along the river; from
around 2016 it added rural and land-based work, including a residential farm
programme outside Delhi.<ref name="about" /><ref name="farm" />

Swechha has also stayed visible in public debate over the Yamuna, taking
journalists and school groups to the river's most degraded stretches in
Delhi — where, as one report of a Swechha visit put it, children asked "where is
the river?"<ref name="zee" /> It has organised walks and clean-up drives on the
river in Delhi and Haryana.<ref name="tribunewalk" />

== Programmes ==

=== Journeys ===
Swechha's ''journeys'' are travelling, residential programmes, usually run with
schools, colleges and companies.

* '''Yamuna Yatra''' — a twelve-day journey of about {{convert|1000|km|mi|abbr=on}} from Yamunotri to Agra, following the river from its clean headwaters to the heavily polluted stretch downstream of Delhi. Swechha says it has run more than thirty of these since 2004, with over 2,000 participants, and that partner schools have included [[Vasant Valley School]], which made the journey part of its Grade XI curriculum.<ref name="about" /><ref name="yatra" /><ref name="twl" />
* '''Gram Anubhav''' — shorter rural immersion journeys of four to five days to villages in Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, built around village interactions, workshops and voluntary labour (''[[shramdaan]]'').<ref name="about" />
* '''Eco-walks''' — half-day guided visits to ecological sites in and around Delhi, including the Yamuna floodplain, the [[Delhi Ridge]], landfills and historic water-harvesting structures.<ref name="about" />

=== Education programmes ===
* '''Bridge the Gap''' — a curriculum-based school programme on land, water, air, waste, climate change and ecology, together with teacher training. Swechha says it has run in more than 250 schools in the Delhi [[National Capital Region (India)|National Capital Region]].<ref name="about" />
* '''Brake Even''' — shorter modular sessions for schools, colleges, companies and institutions.<ref name="about" />
* '''ME to WE''' (earlier ''Pagdandi'') — work with children living and working along the Yamuna, which began in 2007 as an informal school on the riverbank. Under India's [[Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009|Right to Education]] provisions, the programme has helped enrol children from riverside settlements in formal schools; by 2013 about 150 children had been admitted this way.<ref name="twl" /><ref name="about" />
* '''Influence''' and '''CYON''' (Connecting Youth Organisations Nationwide) — college-level volunteering and a network of youth groups across India. Swechha reported working with around forty Delhi colleges and close to 10,000 students annually in the early 2010s.<ref name="twl" /><ref name="about" />

=== Campaigns and events ===
* '''Monsoon Wooding''' — an annual volunteer tree-planting campaign in the Delhi region during the [[monsoon]] months. Swechha states that it plants roughly 5,000 trees a year and that more than 50,000 have been planted and survived in total.<ref name="about" />
* '''Yamuna shramdaan''' — recurring volunteer clean-ups on the river's banks in Delhi. The organisation says it has held these more than twenty-five times, involving tens of thousands of citizens.<ref name="about" /><ref name="lokmarg" />
* Butterfly and herb gardens, and park restoration — Swechha says it has developed more than seventy butterfly parks in the Delhi region, and cites a public park in [[Vasant Kunj]] that it worked on for about a decade as its most substantial park-restoration project.<ref name="about" />
* Youth-led city campaigns on waste, air quality, education rights and civic participation, run through theatre, music and film.<ref name="about" />

=== Farm School ===
Swechha runs a residential learning centre — the Farm School — on farmland
outside Delhi, offering day visits, short courses, internships and stays built
around organic growing, composting, beekeeping and low-impact living.<ref name="farm" /><ref name="about" />

=== Enterprises ===
Swechha operates fair-trade and upcycling enterprises alongside its campaign
work. '''Green the Gap''', later '''Green the Map''', was set up in 2008 to
turn discarded material — juice cartons, vehicle tyres and waste fabric sourced
in Delhi — into bags, wallets, stationery and accessories, with the twin aims of
raising awareness of waste and paying fair wages to workers from disadvantaged
backgrounds.<ref name="idealist" /><ref name="gtm" /> It has operated retail
outlets in Delhi, including at [[Hauz Khas Village]], and supplies buyers in
India and abroad.<ref name="twl" /><ref name="gtm" /> Related ventures include
''Green Creeps'', an urban-farming enterprise begun in 2015, and ''The
Remakery'', a Delhi space for repair, upcycling, barter and performance.<ref name="about" />

== Films ==
Swechha and Jha have produced documentaries on rivers and waste, several of
which have been broadcast in India and abroad. ''[[Jijivisha]]'' (2005) follows
the Yamuna from Yamunotri through Delhi and Agra to [[Prayagraj|Allahabad]];
other titles include ''Wasted'' (2007), ''Disposable'' (2009) and ''Tatva'', on
solid waste and on climate, water and energy.<ref name="jiji" /><ref name="techcamp" />

== Organisation and governance ==
Swechha is a registered society, holding exemptions under sections 12A and 80G
of the [[Income Tax Act, 1961|Income Tax Act]] and registration under the
[[Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010|Foreign Contribution (Regulation)
Act]].<ref name="about" /> It is governed by a governing body, chaired by
Rajeev Singh as president, with Vimlendu Jha as secretary; Jha is also the
organisation's executive director.<ref name="team" /> Swechha lists its
programme funders and partners as having included the [[European Commission]],
[[United Nations Development Programme|UNDP]], [[United Nations Volunteers|UNV]],
[[United Nations Environment Programme|UNEP]], the [[Embassy of the United
States, New Delhi|United States Embassy in New Delhi]], the [[British Council]],
the [[Sir Ratan Tata Trust]] and several companies.<ref name="about" />

== Recognition ==
Recognition has largely attached to the founder. In 2004 Jha was named by the
[[International Youth Foundation]] as one of twenty-five young leaders profiled
in its publication ''Our Time is Now'', and was listed among India's leading
young figures by the magazines ''[[India Today]]'' and ''[[Outlook (Indian magazine)|Outlook]]''.<ref name="techcamp" /><ref name="profile" />
In 2007 CNN International selected him as one of six people worldwide for its
''Be the Change'' series, which reported on his Yamuna work over the following
year.<ref name="cnnbio" /><ref name="cnnriver" /><ref name="cnnarchive" />
He was invited to address a [[United Nations General Assembly]] session on youth
in 2011, has served as a judge for [[NDTV]]'s Green Champion initiative, and has
taken part in the [[United States Department of State]]'s TechCamp
programme.<ref name="profile" /><ref name="ndtv" /><ref name="techcamp" />
